A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AoTD research despite the revised title. Their complete main texts, tables, figures, equations, and Appendices A–D support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original AoTD evaluations, specialized-model measurements, filtering and transferability ablations, and rationale-grounding results.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds VSIBench evaluations, further model-transfer experiments, and inference-cost measurements.

M1.justification: Agent selection, program execution, CoT conversion and verification, the answer/rationale training objective, and prompt-controlled inference remain unchanged. Additional backbone evaluations apply the existing method.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluation-only VSIBench spatial-temporal questions, including multiple-choice and open-ended formats (Tables 3–4). This extends the existing VideoQA coverage while retaining the training datasets and previous benchmarks.

E2.justification: The transferability comparison adds VideoLLaMA2-Instruct and Qwen2-VL-Instruct controls alongside their AoTD variants and removes the untuned Onevision row (v1 Table 6; v2 Table 7). New Table 6 compares the agent system against LNV-AoTD for efficiency. Existing main QA comparator membership is retained.

E3.justification: Table 3 revises MVBench's stated evaluation size from 2.0K to 4.0K; the PDFs do not establish whether evaluation was rerun. Added experiments introduce VSIBench scoring without GPT, two additional backbone settings, and time, memory, and TFLOPs measurements. Existing appendix training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 substantially broadens supplementary validation: transferability testing extends beyond Onevision to VideoLLaMA2 and Qwen2-VL, and a distinct analysis measures the efficiency advantage of distillation over the agent system. The filtering ablation, rationale-grounding evaluation, and appendix examples are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical tests. The unchanged random selection of 200 STAR examples concerns evaluation sampling, not repeated-run uncertainty.

E6.justification: Numerical evidence expands across a new benchmark, additional backbones, and computational costs. Table 4 adds VSIBench scores of 19.7/26.7/28.8 for LNV/Instruct/AoTD and 45.4 for Gemini 1.5 Pro. New Table 6 reports agent/AoTD costs of 47.93/10.58 seconds, 65.34/18.21 GB, and 30.98/13.53 TFLOPs. Further transfer results are added and untuned Onevision results removed; retained score entries are unchanged.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, agent-execution equations, and distillation objective are unchanged. Neither version adds theoretical results, assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the claims that verified agent-generated CoTs improve VideoQA performance and interpretability. The revised title and additional experiments do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly interprets the new latency and computation results as demonstrating the necessity of distillation. It also revises the transferability discussion from testing a single representative model to several. Appendix A's substantive limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures, training hyperparameters, prompts, and the project-access link are unchanged, including Appendices B and D. The new cost table reports outcomes without supplying hardware or measurement implementation details.

R1.justification: v2 adds Yang et al.'s Thinking in Space as reference 43 for VSIBench and its comparison results. The other 54 references and the substantive related-work positioning are retained.

P1.justification: The main title changes from Unlocking Video-LLM via Agent-of-Thoughts Distillation to Enhancing Video-LLM Reasoning via Agent-of-Thoughts Distillation. Brief evaluation explanations and a cost-analysis paragraph are added, with limited wording edits. Section organization and appendix prose remain stable.

P2.justification: Tables 3–4 gain VSIBench entries, a new efficiency table is inserted, and the expanded ablation table is relocated and renumbered from 6 to 7. The grounding table moves and becomes Table 8. Figures and appendix layouts are retained.

improvement.justification: VSIBench and the additional backbone tests strengthen evidence for generalization, while Table 6 quantifies an efficiency advantage previously discussed qualitatively. The net gain is limited: cost measurements lack hardware and workload details, and unchanged superiority language overlooks Gemini's higher VSIBench score of 45.4 versus AoTD's 28.8.
